newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money eases towards close, gilts steady.
newsitem.headline: India call money eases towards close, gilts steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday unchanged from the day's opening levels, in the 9.75-10.0 percent range, after touching 10.50 percent in stray deals, dealers said.
Towards the end of the day, rates came down as some lenders, who had been off the market earlier in the day, came back, dealers said.
"The market is awaiting the monetary policy to be released tomorrow," a foreign bank dealer said. "This should determine the future movement of interest rates."
The Reserve Bank of India releases its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) on October 19.
Dealers said secondary market prices of governemnt securities remained steady in dull trade.

"The market has become cautious in the last three days," a dealer said. "After some speculative trading in the first two weeks of the month, banks have turned cautious and decided to wait till the monetary policy is announced."
The 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded on Friday at 12.72 percent against Thursday's 12.74 while the 13.62 percent 1998 was unchanged at 13.31 percent, dealers said.
A certificate of deposit maturing in March 1997 was traded in the secondary market at a yield of 13.70 percent, they said.
No trades were reported in commercial paper.
Rates on intercorporate deposits were steady in the 18-20 percent range, dealers said.
